gloss: inari sushi; sushi rice in fried tofu pouches

definitions.gloss: inari sushi; sushi rice stuffed in sweetened fried tofu pouches
definitions.explanation: A type of sushi consisting of vinegared rice packed inside pouches of deep-fried tofu (abura-age) that have been simmered in a sweet soy sauce mixture. A popular, affordable everyday sushi often found at convenience stores and bento shops.

examples.japanese: お{弁当|べんとう}に{稲荷寿司|いなりずし}を{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put inari sushi in the lunch box.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}の{作|つく}る{稲荷寿司|いなりずし}は{甘|あま}くて{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: The inari sushi my grandmother makes is sweet and delicious.

examples.japanese: お{花見|はなみ}のとき、{手作|てづく}りの{稲荷寿司|いなりずし}を{持|も}って{行|い}くのが{我|わ}が{家|や}の{習慣|しゅうかん}だ。
examples.english: It's our family tradition to bring homemade inari sushi when we go cherry blossom viewing.

notes:
USAGE:
Named after the Shinto deity {稲荷|いなり}, whose fox messengers are said to be fond of fried tofu. Often shortened to おいなりさん in casual speech, with the honorific さん reflecting affection for the food. It is one of the most common types of sushi eaten at home and is a staple of bento culture.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おいなりさん (casual/affectionate name for inari sushi)
- {稲荷寿司|いなりずし}を{作|つく}る (to make inari sushi)
- {油揚|あぶらあ}げ (fried tofu pouch — the main wrapping ingredient)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手巻|てま}き{寿司|ずし}: hand-rolled sushi — another casual, home-style sushi
- {巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}: rolled sushi — nori-wrapped cylindrical sushi
